morbi.headline: Morbi ceramics faces export losses and fuel cost hikes despite lower container freight rates.
what_changed: Iran war-related disruptions led to a Rs 3,589 crore drop in ceramic exports over six months.
Industrial propane usage resumed, but prices rose by Rs 3/kg to reach Rs 104/kg.
Ocean container freight rates dropped by up to 50 percent, offering relief for exporters.
Local industrialists submitted representations to the district minister regarding power, water, and infrastructure issues.
stress_signals: Export revenue dropped by Rs 3,589 crore in six months due to the war in Iran [19f71f3185bc].
Industrial propane gas price increased by Rs 3 per kg to Rs 104 per kg, clouding recovery prospects [3d9aa30057b8, 9e8c549b7c05].
Ongoing operational challenges reported in electricity supply, water availability, and local infrastructure [8b17a473b62a].
Broader export market challenges and production cost pressures continue to impact tile makers [895aa138960b].
improvement_signals: Ocean container freight rates decreased by up to 50 percent for Morbi ceramics [d6c30857de2c].
what_to_watch: Further escalation in propane gas prices and impact on operating margins of tile manufacturers.
Export order book recovery and sales realizations across Middle East trade routes.
Account-level working capital utilization and overdue trends among export-oriented ceramic units.
Government response and policy action regarding power, water, and infrastructure representations.

surat.headline: Surat cluster exhibits divergence as diamond demand recovers while textiles face liquidity stress.
what_changed: Diamond processing units report improving festive demand and plans for early reopening, despite pre-Diwali rough diamond shortages and historical job cuts.
Textile weaving and trading sub-segments face severe payment delays exceeding 200 days, trade defaults, and collective production cutbacks.
Embroidery labor disputes resolved while MANTRA introduced medical textile testing capabilities in Surat.
stress_signals: Sayan weavers planned a collective vacation to cut fabric production by 60 crore meters over 15 days due to financial distress [297b184838d2].

Weavers staged protests over outstanding payment dues exceeding 200 days, alongside mounting trade defaults including a ₹1.5 crore default to jobworkers [774ba602b06e, 6a3068dc8bf1, 80f44f3f370f, e0787797133b].
SGCCI demanded GUJCTOC application against organized fraud gangs causing multi-crore textile market defaults [421d4bf835f5, f699b1f05b5e].
Pre-Diwali shutdowns in diamond units caused by rough diamond supply shortages, alongside historical reports of 100,000 job losses in the broader downturn [b65b93c4b724, 1bcd949a2599, 9edf027a29a8].
improvement_signals: Diamond cutting factories extending operational hours until Dhanteras and planning early reopening post-vacation on strong demand [e533595d0815, bd78e4a130ff, d6a824e747af].
Lab-grown diamond (LGD) segment experienced rising demand, leading to 10% worker bonuses [751cd1661531].
Textile PLI scheme turnover threshold halved and extended to FY 2033-34, while SGCCI signed two MoUs in Morocco to expand export scope [c7ee55f3effe, 472a28abf217].
what_to_watch: Receivables conversion timelines for powerloom weaving accounts during post-festive settlements.
Rough diamond inventory flow and operational continuity of cutting units post-Dhanteras.
Execution progress on Morocco export MoUs and borrower eligibility under the revised Textile PLI scheme.
